old: Not every ketose disaccharide is reducing; the question is whether an anomeric carbon still has a free –OH. Here fructose C2 is in the glycosidic bond.
new: Free fructose is a reducing sugar, but only because its anomeric C2 has a free –OH that lets the ring open. In sucrose, fructose C2 is tied up in the glycosidic bond.
why: Old feedback rebutted 'every ketose disaccharide', which the choice does not say; free ketoses such as fructose do give positive Benedict's tests, so the real reason must be the blocked anomeric C2
